title: [PC] [Closed beta] CHROMEDRIFT – cyberpunk roguelike deckbuilder, looking for testers who play full runs
author: StitchworkGames
selftext:
Hi! I'm a solo developer from Germany. My deckbuilder CHROMEDRIFT is moving from a public alpha to a **closed beta**, and I'm looking for testers who will actually play it.

**What it is**

A roguelike deckbuilder in the vein of Slay the Spire. You climb a vertical megacity through three acts to reach ARGUS, the AI that runs it. A run takes about 1.5 to 3 hours.

\- Flesh and Net: every enemy has a body and a firewall. Guns and fists hit the Flesh, hacks hit the Net. Break the firewall and the enemy skips its next move and takes 50 % more damage.  
\- Body versus machine: every implant costs Humanity. Your Humanity decides which lines on your cards work, and the story and endings notice what you became.  
\- Nothing hidden: enemies show their next move, and the game shows what a card will do before you play it.

**What is new in the beta**

\- A new look: almost every picture redrawn in a cold, 90s anime film style (film grain, hard shadows, inked lines), with animated scenes.  
\- A second runner: Ryu, the Blade. He has 80 HP, 75 cards of his own, a core that pays him for running hot, and his own story and endings.  
\- The game teaches itself: your first run brings in the rules one fight at a time, and your runner explains each new idea in one short line.  
\- More to do: five alarm levels after your first win, a daily run, controller and Steam Deck support.

**What I'm asking**

\- Play at least one full run, ideally more than one.  
\- Tell me honestly what worked and what didn't. A short questionnaire comes with the build.  
\- Windows 10/11 (64-bit), or a Steam Deck. English or German.

**How to join**

Leave a comment under this post or wirte me a DM. The beta is not public; the old alpha stays free to download: [https://stitchworkgames.itch.io/chromedrift](https://stitchworkgames.itch.io/chromedrift)

**Honest note:** the illustrations, music and sound effects were made with AI tools and reworked by hand, and I code with AI assistance. Design, rules, balancing and story are mine. Nothing is generated while you play.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Feedback: 

First, this game is great. I hope I ever make something this nice.

  
Quality of Life / Bugs: 

 \- The Patch screen looks very nice, but the interaction is quite ugly - hovering over a card changes the target to be patched, so what you have to do as the player is hover over the card you want to patch, then weave your mouse around to avoid hovering over anything else, then click the Apply button. 

I think this could be solved by either letting the player lock-in their selection by clicking it, so the hover doesn't change the target, or just getting rid of the apply button in the preview window and making it a function on the card itself. 

 \- It would be nice if there was a toggle in the deck view and, when being asked to choose a reward card, to see what the Patch upgrade is for that card. 

 \- The game needs to provide much clearer feedback on triggers and modifiers. The Chimera augment is the worst offender here - it's an incredibly cool augment, but it is never clear about when it will fire. Even a simple tag on cards that says 'Chimera' or something if/when the effect would apply would be very helpful.

 \- Damage previews, if you're going to include them, should display damage after modifiers are taken into account. Being lied to about a preview is extremely feelsbadman.

  
Opinions About My Experience:

 \- ICE as an effect just rarely seems worth it for the player to pick up right now. I almost always skip anything whose primary function is adding ICE, and cut the basic ICE cards from the deck as soon as I can. 

 \- It feels like there aren't quite enough Unwired enemies, which makes the (admittedly limited) pool of cards that trigger specifically against Unwired enemies seem fairly underpowered. IMHO, I think the best solution here is to just cut the cards that specifically target Unwired enemies rather than adding more Unwired enemies. 

 \- The Black Market prices seem too expensive to me. The primary problem is that because the prices are so high, there's no point in going to the shop in the early game, IMHO. 

 \- The jobs you pick-up each Act are neat... but there's not enough feedback about the payoff to make it feel good. IMHO, it would be great if there was a clear progress tracker that populates every time the player pushes ahead on the job, and also nice if the job just paid out upon completion rather than forcing the player to wait until the boss is cleared (which makes most of the Act 3 jobs feel pointless). 

 \- The overall power curve feels a bit off. On one hand, the individual cards have a very conservative design, especially for Uncommons and Rares, which doesn't make them feel very exciting to pick up. On the other hand, in aggregate, the player becomes overwhelmingly powerful by the end of Act 3 because of how ridiculous some of the Augments and/or Instinct upgrades are. The power level feels about right for Act 1 and Act 2, but the snowball is in full effect for Act 3 and I just mulch the fights there. I think individual Uncommon / Rare cards should be more exciting to draft, while at the same time the overall power level of the player should be tamed a bit (...though, in fairness, this same snowballing effect happens in literally all deckbuilders, so it's not exactly the worst thing in the world. It's just that right now in Chromedrift it feels a bit like it happens too often).   
  
 \- Acts feels just a hair too long for my liking. Part of it is that fights are more involved, so each individual fight takes longer than something like StS (though this becomes less of a thing when the player is in full belnder mode in Act 3). I think I'd prefer them if they were compressed into maybe 2/3rds of their current length.  
  
  \- The two characters don't have enough of an identity split right now, IMHO. I think part of this is how the baseline systems of the game already have a lot of diversity built into them, so unique mechanics per character have a harder time shining through. This is an area where I would take a look at some fundamental structure. If Blade wants Heat to be his thing... maybe Heat should only be Blade's thing, rather than a thing Dive also has but he can use it a bit better? 

  
Best of luck with this project.
